analyst_view.overall: Mid-table, level on 12 points: Hoffenheim (11th) host Augsburg (10th) on Sunday evening. Hoffenheim came back to beat Sturm Graz 3-1 in the Europa League on Thursday with goals from substitutes, but Wouter Burger limped off and is a doubt, and their defence is stripped: Ozan Kabak is banned, and Robin Hranáč (knee operation, weeks out), Albian Hajdari, Valentin Gendrey and Nathan De Cat are injured; the numbers list them but only add for Kabak. Augsburg ended a seven-game winless run by beating Mainz 3-1 (Gregoritsch twice, seven league goals), had a full week off, and coach Manuel Baum was sent off in that game, so he is banned from the bench; their injury list (Gouweleeuw, Massengo, Matsima, Mounié, Banks, Sakar) comes from the brief and could not be rechecked. Dr. Matthias Jöllenbeck referees (counted). News was thin: no dedicated preview for this match was found.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals and already add about 6% to Augsburg for Kabak's ban. They don't add anything for Hranáč, who now needs weeks after a knee operation rather than returning in late November, or for Hajdari, leaving Christian Ilzer without his usual centre-backs against an Augsburg side that has scored 12 in six. Augsburg's own back line is patched up too, so I add a small 3%, to about 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners and already count recent corner form (Hoffenheim forcing plenty, Augsburg conceding few). Hoffenheim's switch to a 4-2-3-1 in Graz and Wimmer's return don't change their wide play much, so I stay at 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards and already add for both teams' recent bookings and for Jöllenbeck (5.2 a game, but from only four games). Augsburg's last game was heated enough for Baum to be sent off, and he will be off the bench here, but there is no rivalry, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.2 shots, already well above average because both teams have been shooting a lot (Augsburg 118 in six, +21%). Hoffenheim's Thursday game and Burger's knock could cost them a little, while their makeshift defence may let Augsburg shoot more; these roughly cancel, so I stay at 34.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target and already add for Augsburg's sharp recent shooting (40 on target in six). Hoffenheim's thin back line could allow a few more clear chances, but I have put that into goals, so I stay at 10.6.
